facts.text: The trail's eastern end. There's no road access, so most people start a few miles west at Black Walnut.
The easternmost trailhead with parking, about three miles from the trail's end at Machens.
Missouri's first state capital, and the last stop for Lewis and Clark's expedition before it headed up the Missouri in May 1804.
Near a former uranium processing site. You can climb its capped disposal cell for a view over the river valley.
Daniel Boone spent his last years nearby. His family's stone house is north of the trail, off Highway F.

facts.title: Klondike Park
facts.text: A former silica sand quarry, now a county park with bluff-top views of the Missouri River.
In 1980 Augusta became the first federally recognized wine region in the United States.
Settled by German immigrants in 1832, it's considered the oldest German town in Missouri.
Daniel and Rebecca Boone were first buried near here, before their remains were moved to Kentucky.
Hermann sits just across the river, an easy detour over the Route 19 bridge.
Home to a trail shelter that offers simple bunkhouse lodging for trail users.
A bike and pedestrian lane on the Missouri River bridge links the trail here with Jefferson City and the Capitol.
